item.title: The 1-Loop and Ohtsuki-Takata Invariants for Alternating Braids
item.description: arXiv:2611.26790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a step towards resolving the 1-loop conjecture, Ohtsuki and Takata defined their own eponymous invariant in terms of an open knot diagram, and showed that it is equal to the adjoint Reidemeister torsion for two-bridge knots. Garoufalidis and Yoon then showed that the 1-loop invariant is equal to the Ohtsuki-Takata invariant using a technique involving a collapsed octahedral decomposition. This paper expands those techniques to relate the matrix determinants of the 1-loop and Ohtsuki-Takata invariants for the case of reduced alternating braids.
item.dc:creator: Alexander R. Pierson

item.title: The Strong AJ Conjecture for Hyperbolic Prime Knots is False
item.description: arXiv:2611.26905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. The strong AJ conjecture relates two of its invariants. The first is the minimal-order annihilator $\widehat A$ of the $n$th colored Jones polynomial $J(n)$. The second is the two-variable $A$-polynomial of Cooper, Culler, Gillet, Long, and Shalen. The conjecture says that after specialization $\varepsilon^*(\widehat A)\asymp A$. Zhang gave the first family of composite-knot counterexamples. For $8_{11}$ the specialization of $\widehat A$ carries an extra trefoil factor $L+M^6$. We prove this by verifying L\^e's $\widehat P=\widehat A$ conjecture. Zhang's corrected formulation of the AJ conjecture agrees with L\^e's weak AJ conjecture, which we prove for $8_{11}$. Li, Li, and Sun have since reported counterexamples of the weak AJ conjecture among non-hyperbolic prime knots. This work was AI assisted, and parts of it have been formalized in Lean.
item.dc:creator: RJ Acu\~na

item.title: There are hard braids
item.description: arXiv:2611.27472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let us call a trivial braid hard if it cannot be untangled by Reidemeister moves without increasing the number of crossings. Are there hard trivial braids? Our paper answers this question. Hard braids exist. For every number of strands starting from 4, for every even length starting from 16, we present examples of hard trivial braids of that size. Our smallest example is minimal. We prove that there are no hard braids on three strands. On four strands our shortest example, of length 16, is a shortest hard braid. The hard braids in that family can be untangled without increasing their length if we use Reidemeister moves and an infinite family of moves $\sigma_i^{\varepsilon}\sigma_j^{m}\sigma_i^{-\varepsilon} \leftrightarrow\sigma_j^{-\varepsilon}\sigma_i^{m}\sigma_j^{\varepsilon}$, which involve only three strands. We also build a harder family of hard braids which no moves confined to a bounded number of strands can untangle. For every $m$ we construct a trivial braid on $4m$ strands, of length $16m^2$, which can be untangled without increasing its length by moves on $2m+1$ strands but not not on $2m$ strands.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Vernitski

item.title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2611.27926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as K\'alm\'an, Lilla T\'othm\'er\'esz

item.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.26229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $\Delta^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matou\v{s}ek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Norin

item.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
item.description: arXiv:2611.19217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,\xi)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author. Finally, we use Luttinger twists along the Klein bottle to construct contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings, without the use of open books or Lefschetz fibrations.
item.dc:creator: Burak Ozbagci

item.title: Monodromy factorizations of lines on del Pezzo surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2503.23382v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a list of monodromy factorizations in the pure mapping class group $PMod(T_{d+1})$ of a torus with d+1 marked points that represent lines on a del Pezzo surface Y of degree $d\le4$. These factorizations are lifts of a certain fixed monodromy factorization in $PMod(T_d)$ that represents Y. In the case d=1, discussed in more detail, we give an explicit correspondence between such factorizations and the 240 roots of $E_8=K^\perp$, the orthogonal complement in $H_2(Y)$ of the canonical class.
item.dc:creator: Mohan Bhupal, Sergey Finashin
